name: SHA-1 Hash
summary: Compute a SHA-1 digest of text in your browser — for legacy checksums, not new security designs.
description: Hash UTF-8 text with a pure SHA-1 implementation and copy the hex digest. SHA-1 is cryptographically broken for collision resistance; prefer SHA-256 for security-sensitive work. Nothing is uploaded.

faqs.question: Is SHA-1 secure?
faqs.answer: No for collision-resistant uses (signatures, certificates). It can still appear in legacy checksums. Use SHA-256 for new designs.

faqs.question: How is text encoded before hashing?
faqs.answer: As UTF-8 bytes, matching common tooling.

faqs.question: Is my input uploaded?
faqs.answer: No. Hashing runs entirely in your browser.
